A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same narrow-width Bayesian branching-network study. The graph model and Figures 1–8 match, and the complete text, equations, figures, and appendices support comparison, including v3's added general-architecture appendix.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–5 report original Hamiltonian Monte Carlo experiments on CSBM student-teacher tasks and binary Cora regression, compared with theoretical predictions.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original residual-MLP experiments on synthetic Gaussian data and binary CIFAR-10 in Appendix B, Figures 9–16.

M1.justification: The original graph architecture is retained under the name BPB-GCN. Appendix B adds general branch feature maps and a residual-MLP with independent linear and ReLU branches, substantively extending the model beyond the original linear graph-convolution branches.

E1.justification: v2 evaluates CSBM student-teacher regression and binary Cora regression. v3 retains both and adds student-teacher regression on independent Gaussian vectors and airplane-versus-cat CIFAR-10 classification formulated as regression, extending coverage beyond graph data.

E2.justification: The finite-width versus wide-width/GP comparison is retained and extended to the added experiments. No external comparator is added or removed from a reported experiment; newly cited PAC-Bayes, CNN, and ResNet work is discussed rather than evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendices C.3–C.4 introduce residual-MLP protocols using 1,280 training and 320 test Gaussian examples, and red-channel CIFAR-10 with 1,000 training and 1,000 test examples, plus task-specific temperatures and prior sweeps. Original graph protocols are retained; the newly stated CSBM split is additional disclosure rather than evidence of a changed experiment.

E4.justification: Figures 9–16 add substantial analyses of width and prior sensitivity, student-teacher branch-norm recovery, and bias–variance tradeoffs for residual-MLPs. The CIFAR-10 analyses additionally examine linear-versus-ReLU branch contributions and variance-dominated generalization. The original graph analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report HMC averages and posterior-variance curves without run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or uncertainty bars for the estimated results. v3 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation procedure. Its discussion of correlated CIFAR-10 samples is a limitation disclosure.

E6.justification: Figures 1–8 retain identical plotted results. New Figures 9–16 report residual-MLP branch-norm recovery and CIFAR-10 ReLU dominance. Figure 16 shows that narrower CIFAR-10 networks have higher accuracy from averaged predictions but higher overall mean-squared error because of variance. These are substantial new results under added settings.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 replaces the assumption-dependent equipartition conjecture with an asserted theorem under explicit zero-temperature and limiting-width conditions, revises its proof, and removes v2's branch-output recovery derivation in Eq. 24. Appendix B adds a generalized theorem, while Appendix A.2 revises and expands the partition-function derivation.

C1.justification: v2 centers its main contributions on BPB-GNNs while suggesting broader relevance. v3's abstract, introduction contribution 4, and conclusion explicitly claim the narrow-width effect as a general feature of Bayesian parallel branching networks, including residual-MLPs. This substantially broadens the claimed contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds an absence-of-oversmoothing interpretation, an explanation involving CIFAR-10 ReLU dominance, and ensembling as a variance-reduction strategy. Its limitations introduce lazy-versus-rich learning regimes and possible failure of the bias advantage under online learning, substantially extending v2's variance and Bayesian-to-SGD caveats. Appendix C.4 also attributes CIFAR-10 bias discrepancies to correlated samples.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly specifies 2,600 CSBM nodes and a 65% training fraction, supplies configurations for the added experiments, and discloses Nvidia A100-40G hardware and a 20 GPU-hour budget. These expand reproducibility information, while the HMC implementation description and original sampling-width limits remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 reframes novelty from a tight generalization bound to an a priori bias–variance decomposition for linear residual-like GCNs, explicitly contrasting PAC-Bayes approaches by Liao et al. and Ju et al. The discussion substantially expands positioning through CNN kernel renormalization, ResNet ensembles, and lazy/rich learning-regime literature.

P1.justification: The title and BPB-NN/BPB-GCN terminology change, and introductory and concluding passages are revised. Main-text predictor formulas already present in Appendix A.3 are replaced with cross-references, and experimental Appendix B becomes C. Despite these edits, the main section sequence and much of the existing exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 9–16, substantially expanding the visual presentation with residual-MLP branch-norm, bias, variance, total-error, and accuracy plots. Figures 1–8 retain identical graphics; other changes include caption terminology, page reflow, and conference headers.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful nonlinear and CIFAR-10 evidence, experimental specifications, and more informative limitations. However, v2 explicitly qualified teacher-output concentration as an assumption; v3 Eq. 19 invokes the law of large numbers without establishing that a single teacher's output outer product concentrates at its ensemble covariance, then labels the result a theorem. Appendix B further generalizes it while nonlinear kernel renormalization remains conjectural. The empirical gains and reduced mathematical qualification leave the net quality change uncertain.
